references.text: Moses expresses the wish that Israel would understand and know their situation: 'Oh that they were wise, that they understood this, that they considered their future!' (Deut 32:29). Jesus expresses a similar sorrow over Jerusalem not knowing what leads to peace.

Isaiah prophesies about a people who see but do not understand, and hear but do not perceive (Isa 6:9-10). Jerusalem was blinded and could not recognize what leads to peace—it was 'hidden from their eyes'.

'Oh that you had paid attention to my commandments! Then your peace would have been like a river' (Isa 48:18). The Lord's lament over Israel's failure to listen, and thus missing out on peace, corresponds directly with Jesus weeping over Jerusalem for not knowing what leads to peace.
The Lord has closed the eyes of the prophets and covered the heads of those who see (Isa 29:10). This parallels the truth now being 'hidden from your eyes' in Jesus' words over Jerusalem.
Jeremiah weeps in secret over Israel's pride and captivity (Jer 13:17). Jesus' weeping over Jerusalem recalls Jeremiah's sorrow over the fate of his people.
'How can I give you up, Ephraim? How can I hand you over, Israel?' (Hos 11:8). God's deep grief and reluctance to judge His people is mirrored in Jesus' lament over Jerusalem.

Jesus laments over Jerusalem: 'Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you who kill the prophets and stone those sent to you! How often would I have gathered your children' (Matt 23:37). The same deep sorrow over the city that refuses to accept salvation.
Paul writes that 'a part of Israel has been hardened' (Rom 11:25). The blindness that has come upon Israel, that what leads to peace is 'hidden from their eyes', is linked to this hardening.
Paul writes that 'a veil lies over their heart' when the Law of Moses is read (2 Cor 3:14-15). This corresponds with what led to peace being hidden from Jerusalem's eyes.

Jesus laments over Jerusalem for killing the prophets and says their house will be left desolate (Luke 13:34-35). An earlier lament by Jesus over the city, pointing forward to Luke 19:42 and the coming judgment.
